I agree with others that keeping paper logging forms in the OB van is reasonable, although as we often see, bigger outside broadcasts tend to have a mixture of presenters and helpers, in which case we typically choose the simplest clip-board sheet for the station.

Occasionally, I run into issues with unexpected receipts or ad-hoc expenses, and then find that Coast FM or Radio St Ives have found a workable template for it, and I adopt that. When I've already spent some hours getting an expense sheet working for Sallow FM, I want it to be usable as widely as possible by everyone on the team with as little fuss as possible. text:
I read your previous email and I fully agree with you on that, but I
disagree with your conclusion (second sentence of your above).

For the record: I disagree strongly with the idea that Tuesday evening pre-records
in general don't require itemised log entries.

The reason I disagree with your conclusion has to do with a broadcast
consisting of multiple segments, where some segments may be both easily
identifiable and also not in themselves require PPL clearance. Local acoustic sessions
consist of such a subset, which has a third feature of being
potentially exempt from standard licensing: live in-studio improvisations.

(please see my response to Chloe for more details on that reasoning)

Initially I talked about full show logs, but then I shifted to talk
more narrowly about the subset of "studio-session/*" tracks, and that is what
you quoted. Your position I fully agree with, but I am unsure if you
really mean that it holds true also for acoustic session tracks as a subset on
their own - and I suspect that I would disagree with such a position.

Do you insist so very strongly that live session takes must have full ISRCs logged?
